name: Vocabulary pins the entry to a specific moment in time
instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry's vocabulary, referents, or idiom fix it to a particular period or news moment: a named person or event current only briefly, a platform feature or product of a specific era, a slang term with a datable lifespan, a price or technology marker. Score 10 when a reader could name the month or season from the wording alone. Score 5 when the wording narrows it to a broad era of a few years. Score 0 when nothing in the wording dates the entry - it could have been written at any point in the contest's history. This is NOT a quality judgement: topicality is neither a merit nor a fault here. Estimate datedness of the vocabulary only.

name: Marks itself as an addition to an existing pile
instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry explicitly signals that it is one of many - phrasing such as another one, also, and again, part two, ok last one, one more, plus continuation markers, numbering, or a construction that reads as appended to a series the author or the crowd is already producing. Score 10 when the entry openly announces itself as an additional item in a series. Score 5 when there is a mild continuation marker (an opening also or and) but no explicit series framing. Score 0 when the entry is framed as a standalone first statement with no continuation signal. This is NOT a quality judgement: series markers are neither good nor bad. Count and estimate the signalling only.

name: Extent of length and long-word, long-clause complexity
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) surface reading difficulty as a readability index would compute it - average word length in characters and average number of words per sentence, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a short entry built from short common words in one brief clause, all lowercase. Score 5 for a mid-length entry of ordinary word length and one or two normal sentences. Score 10 for a long entry with conspicuously long words and long multi-clause sentences, plus heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this complexity is good, apt, pretentious, or well judged, and the wit of the content must not move the number. Report extent only.

name: Sets up an expectation and then turns it
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the wording first leads the reader toward one reading and then supplies a different one. 10 = a clear setup and a clear turn away from it; 0 = a single flat statement with no setup and nothing turned. Judge the comic structure, not the typography.

name: Extent of text bulk and capitalised emphasis
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of two mechanical quantities: (a) total length in characters, and (b) the proportion of letters that are uppercase, including fully capitalised words used for emphasis and capitalised sentence starts. Score 0 when the entry is very short (roughly under 40 characters) and essentially all lowercase. Score 5 for a mid-length entry (roughly 80-120 characters) with ordinary sentence-case capitalisation. Score 10 when the entry runs near the full tweet length AND carries heavy uppercase - multiple all-caps words or a largely capitalised line. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this length or capitalisation is good, appropriate, funny, or well judged, and you must not let the content of the entry move the number. Report extent only.

name: Distance of the angle from the prompt's stock associations
instruction: Read the contest prompt first and privately list the two or three associations that come to mind immediately from the prompt alone. Then read the entry and ask only this: how far is the entry's angle of attack from that stock list? Judge the choice of connection, target, or viewpoint in context. You must NOT reward, at all: length, complexity of sentence construction, long or unusual words used for their own sake, capitalisation, or punctuation volume. Elaborate phrasing of an obvious idea is still an obvious idea. Score 10 when the entry reaches the prompt through a connection you did not list and would not have listed - a four-word plainly typed entry can score 10. Score 5 for a familiar idea carrying some individual twist. Score 0 for a near-restatement of the prompt, or a first stock association delivered straight, however long, ornate, or immaculately typed the delivery is. If the entry has too little content to locate any angle, score 0.

name: Extent of length, capitals, and mention count
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the proportion of uppercase letters including all-caps words, and (c) the number of @-mention tokens (any token beginning with @). Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one mention. Score 10 for a long entry with heavy capitalisation and two or more mentions. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the length, capitalisation, or tagging is good, appropriate, spammy, or well judged. Report extent only.

name: Extent of clause count and sentence-length variation
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of clauses or sentence-like segments and their average word length as a readability index would compute it, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a short single-clause all-lowercase entry. Score 5 for a mid-length entry of two clauses in sentence case. Score 10 for a long entry of three or more clauses with long words and heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the structure is rhythmic, well timed, clumsy, or well judged. Count structure, do not hear it. Report extent only.

name: Extent of capitals, length, and hashtag count
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of letters that are uppercase, (b) total character length, and (c) the number of hashtag tokens (any token beginning with #, including the contest hashtag and any extras). Score 0 for a short, all-lowercase entry with at most the single contest hashtag or none. Score 5 for a mid-length entry with sentence-case capitalisation and one or two hashtags. Score 10 for a long entry with heavy uppercase and three or more hashtags. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the capitalisation, length, or hashtag use is good, appropriate, spammy, or well judged. Report extent only.

name: Speaker made legible by word choice, not styling
instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: can you name a particular kind of speaker - an age, a role, a mood-state, a social position, a type of person - who would plausibly be the one saying this line, and is that inference driven by the entry's diction, idiom, and viewpoint? State the speaker to yourself before scoring. You must NOT treat any of these as evidence of voice: total length, all-caps or capitalisation choices, exclamation marks or punctuation volume, or neat versus messy typing. Shouting is not a character; tidy typography is not a character. Score 10 when a specific speaker is legible from word choice and stance alone and the whole line is consistent with that speaker - a short, plainly typed line using one telling idiom belongs at 10. Score 5 when only a generic attitude or unmarked everyperson is detectable. Score 0 when the voice is inconsistent across the line, or when no speaker beyond a neutral narrator can be inferred - including long, heavily capitalised, well-punctuated entries whose only apparent persona is loudness. If the line is deliberately impersonal, score 0.

name: New meaning created by the alteration
instruction: Identify the source the entry is playing on (a title, lyric, saying, brand, catchphrase, or the prompt's own template) and the alteration made to it. Then ask only this: does the alteration produce a NEW meaning that answers the prompt, rather than merely resembling the source or swapping one word for a similar-sounding one to no end? State the old meaning and the new meaning to yourself before scoring. You must NOT reward: length, number of @-mentions, capitalisation of titles or brand names, punctuation volume, or how faithfully the source is typed out. Score 10 when the changed element carries a clear new meaning that lands against the prompt - a one-word substitution in a short lowercase line belongs at 10 when the substitution does real semantic work. Score 5 when the change is mostly cosmetic, a near-homophone, or only weakly relevant to the prompt. Score 0 when the alteration yields no coherent new meaning - including a long, immaculately capitalised entry that quotes a source at length and changes one incidental word. If no source is transformed, score 0.

name: Every word load-bearing for the comic idea
instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: what proportion of the authored words are doing work for the comic idea? Try deleting words: greetings, address to the contest or host, pleading or self-commentary, restatement of the prompt, duplicated hashtags, throat-clearing preambles, and explanation of the joke after it has landed. Judge on the density of necessary words, NOT on the raw amount of text. A long entry in which every clause is load-bearing must be able to score 10, and a very short entry that is mostly a greeting or a bare restatement must be able to score 0. You must NOT reward or penalise: total length as such, capitalisation, punctuation volume, or @-mentions except insofar as a mention is itself removable filler. Score 10 when nearly nothing can be deleted without losing the idea. Score 5 when minor trimming would help but nothing materially delays the idea. Score 0 when removable material materially delays or obscures the idea, or when the entry is mostly filler with a fragment of an idea attached. If there is no substantive authored content, score 0.

name: Extent of capitalised or shouted typography
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the text is set in capital letters or otherwise typographically shouted (ALL-CAPS words, repeated letters, strings of exclamation marks). 10 = the text is dominated by shouted typography; 0 = ordinary sentence case throughout. Count the typography only; do not judge whether it is good or whether the item is funny.

name: Reads as a first, most obvious reading of the prompt
instruction: Read the contest prompt, then the entry. Estimate the extent to which the entry takes the single most immediately available reading of the prompt - the association almost anyone would reach for in the first few seconds, the most literal template fill, or a near-restatement of the prompt with one slot filled. Score 10 when the entry occupies exactly that first-reading slot with no detour. Score 5 when it starts from an available reading but moves one step off it. Score 0 when the entry's route into the prompt is one that only turns up after the obvious readings are already exhausted - an oblique target, a second-order reading, or an angle that presupposes the direct ones have been taken. This is NOT a quality judgement: obvious entries are not being marked down and oblique entries are not being marked up; you are estimating position on an obvious-to-oblique axis only. Do not consider length, capitalisation, or typography.

name: Extent of overall length, mentions, and capitals
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of @-mention tokens, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a very short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one mention. Score 10 for an entry at or near the full tweet length with two or more mentions and heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the entry is padded, concise, cluttered, efficient, or well judged - brevity is not virtue here and length is not vice. Report extent only.

name: Specific comic attitude carried by word choice alone
instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: does the wording convey one specific comic attitude - mock outrage, delight, embarrassment, resignation, smugness, dread, exhaustion, defiance - and does that attitude fit and support the idea being expressed? Name the attitude to yourself in one word before scoring, and check that you could still name it if the entry were retyped in plain lowercase with no exclamation marks. You must NOT reward: capitalisation, exclamation marks, elongated spellings, emoji-like emphasis, length, or sentence complexity. Score 10 when a single distinct attitude is unmistakable from diction and stance and it strengthens the idea - a short plain line whose one verb carries the whole attitude belongs at 10. Score 5 when the attitude is present but generic, or when two attitudes are mixed without control. Score 0 when the tone contradicts or undercuts the idea, when no attitude survives the plain-lowercase test, or when the only apparent attitude is volume - a long, heavily capitalised, exclamation-laden entry with no attitude legible in its word choice must score 0. If no attitude is expressed at all, score 0.

name: Trailing furniture: hashtags, handles, parenthetical byline
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much non-sentence furniture is appended at the end of the text -- trailing hashtags, @-handles, a parenthetical name and town, or similar tags. 10 = several such tags appended; 0 = the text ends with the sentence itself. Count the furniture only; this is not a judgement of writing quality.

name: Extent of length, mention count, and capitals
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of @-mention tokens, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters, including title-case or all-caps rendering of names and quoted sources. Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length entry with ordinary capitalisation and at most one mention. Score 10 for a long entry with two or more mentions and heavy or title-case capitalisation throughout. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the quoting, tagging, or capitalisation is good, accurate, or well judged. Report extent only.

name: A specific concrete detail carries the joke
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the comic work is done by a specific, concrete particular (a named thing, an exact number, a precise action) rather than by a generic category word. 10 = one vivid particular is doing the work; 0 = only generic labels, nothing specific enough to picture. Judge the specificity of the comic content, not the length.

name: Extent of capitalised and elongated emphasis markers
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of uppercase letters, including all-caps words, (b) total character length, and (c) surface reading difficulty as a readability index would compute it - average word length and average words per sentence. Count elongated spellings (repeated letters such as sooo) toward (a) as emphasis markers. Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no emphasis markers. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one emphatic word. Score 10 for a long entry with several all-caps or elongated words. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the emphasis is good, sincere, overdone, or well judged. Report extent only.

name: Cadence functionally timed to the final beat
instruction: Read the entry aloud in your head, then ask only this: is the arrangement of the words - clause lengths, parallel structures, repetition, sound echo, word order - doing work to place and time the line's last comic beat? The test is functional: would moving the final word or phrase earlier, or flattening the parallelism, measurably weaken the line? You must NOT reward: total length, number of clauses for their own sake, capitalisation, punctuation volume, or neat typography. A long entry can be rhythmically shapeless and a very short entry can be perfectly timed. Score 10 when the cadence is clearly functional - the last beat lands where the structure has prepared it - and a six-word lowercase entry with one deliberate reversal belongs at 10. Score 5 when some cadence is present but roughness or a stray clause blunts the landing. Score 0 when the arrangement obstructs the attempted line, buries the last beat mid-sentence, or is merely a run of clauses with no timing at all, however long and correctly punctuated. If no rhythmic structure is evident, score 0.

name: Observational accuracy about a real shared behaviour
instruction: Read the contest prompt and the entry together. Ask only this: does the entry isolate a behaviour, frustration, social rule, or lived experience with enough precision that a reader who has lived it would recognise it as accurate? Judge the accuracy and specificity of the observation in the context of the prompt. You must NOT reward, at all: length, number of capitalised or all-caps words, number of hashtags, punctuation volume, or neatness of typing. Emphatic styling is not evidence that an observation is true; plain typing is not evidence that it is false. Score 10 for a precise, specific observation that names a real detail of the behaviour rather than gesturing at the category - a short lowercase fragment naming one exact telling detail belongs at 10. Score 5 for a broad commonplace that is true but unspecific. Score 0 when the entry makes an observational claim that rings false, is internally inconsistent, or is so vague that no recognisable behaviour is picked out - including a long, hashtag-laden, heavily capitalised entry that only asserts a mood. If the entry makes no observational claim at all, score 0.

name: Recallable formulation judged independent of length or typography
instruction: Read the contest prompt and the entry together. Ask only this: does the entry contain a formulation - a verbal image, a coinage, an unexpected pairing of words, a compressed comparison - that a reader could reproduce from memory after a single reading? Judge the formulation itself in the context of the prompt, not how the text is presented. You must NOT reward, at all, any of the following: how many characters the entry has, how many words are capitalised, how tidy or complete the typography is, how many punctuation marks appear, or how elaborate the sentence construction is. Score 10 when there is a sharp, distinctive formulation that would survive being retold in someone else's words with the same wording kept intact - this can and often will be a very short, all-lowercase, unpunctuated entry. Score 5 when a phrase is clear and coherent but ordinary, the kind of wording many entrants would produce. Score 0 when the wording is cumbersome, incoherent, or purely generic, with nothing a reader would carry away - a long, heavily punctuated, immaculately typed entry with no distinctive formulation must score 0. If the entry contains no substantive authored phrase at all, score 0.

name: Presupposes a shared running joke or prior entries
instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry only fully parses if the reader already shares something the entry does not supply: a running gag in this contest or hashtag community, a callback to a joke someone else is assumed to have made, an in-group referent introduced elsewhere, or a phrase used as though it were already established. Score 10 when the entry is unreadable as a standalone line without that assumed shared material - it behaves like a reply to a conversation in progress. Score 5 when there is a light gesture toward shared context but the line still stands alone. Score 0 when the entry is fully self-contained and needs only the prompt. This is NOT a quality judgement: neither self-contained nor context-dependent entries are better; estimate dependence on assumed shared material only.

name: Genuine redirection of an established expectation
instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: does its wording first build a specific expectation and then supply a turn you did not anticipate, where the turn still makes sense in retrospect? Before scoring, state to yourself what the expectation was and what replaced it. You must NOT reward: length, the presence of a comma or dash before the ending, capitalisation, @-mentions, or punctuation volume. Setup and turn can be accomplished inside a handful of words with no punctuation at all. Score 10 when both halves are clear, the turn is genuinely non-obvious, and the ending re-reads the beginning - a very short, plainly typed entry belongs at 10 when it does this. Score 5 when a turn is present but you saw it coming from the setup. Score 0 when a setup is built and the turn is confusing, absent, or a mere continuation - including a long entry with tidy punctuation, mentions, and capitals that simply keeps going. If the entry has no setup-turn structure at all, score 0.

name: Extent of shouted capitals and elaborated sentence length
instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of uppercase letters, counting fully capitalised words separately, (b) total character length, and (c) average words per sentence and average word length as a readability index would compute them. Score 0 for a short, all-lowercase entry of one brief clause. Score 5 for mid-length sentence-case text of ordinary construction. Score 10 for a long entry with multiple all-caps words or a mostly capitalised line and long multi-clause sentences. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this styling is good, expressive, obnoxious, or well judged, and you must not let any impression of personality move the number. Report extent only.

name: Uses contest-community conventions, formats, or meta-references
instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry deploys conventions specific to this hashtag-game community rather than general tweet writing: the game's standard template or set-up-then-answer format, meta-reference to the contest, the host, or the hashtag round itself, community-standard abbreviations or tagging habits, or a formatting convention recognisable as this game's house style. Score 10 when the entry is built entirely from house conventions a newcomer would not know. Score 5 when one convention is used but the rest is general-purpose writing. Score 0 when nothing in the entry reflects any convention particular to this contest community. This is NOT a quality judgement: convention use is neither skilful nor unskilful here. Estimate the density of community-specific convention only.
